title: Claim Qualification Standards — Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance
content:
The measures below set, for each tier of Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance, the thresholds a long-term care claim on an Ashgrove CareAssure policy is measured against: how many activities of daily living the insured must be unable to perform, which activities are recognized, how long the loss of capacity must be expected to last, how recent the practitioner certification must be, how often chronic illness is recertified, and the elimination period.

| Standard | 2-Year | 3-Year | 4-Year | 5-Year | 6-Year | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Activities of daily living the insured must be unable to perform | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Period the loss of capacity must be expected to last | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days |
| Practitioner certification dated within, before the claim decision | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months |
| Recertification of chronic illness while benefits continue, every | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months | 12 months |
| Elimination period (days of chronic illness, satisfied once per lifetime) | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days | 90 days |
| Window within which non-consecutive elimination days may accumulate | 730 days | 730 days | 730 days | 730 days | 730 days | 730 days |

**Activities of daily living recognized in every tier:** bathing, continence, dressing, eating, toileting and transferring — six activities.

### Reading the measures

- *Two of six.* The count is a minimum: an insured unable to perform 2 of the six recognized activities meets the count, and so does an insured unable to perform 3 or more; an insured unable to perform only 1 does not meet it.
- *Expected duration.* The loss of capacity must be expected to last at least 90 days; an expected duration of 89 days falls short.
- *Certification age.* A certification dated 12 months or less before the claim decision is within the period; one dated earlier than that is not.
- *Elimination days.* The 90 days of chronic illness need not be consecutive, provided they fall within a 730-day window; the period is satisfied once in the insured's lifetime.

### Illustration (hypothetical days)

An insured who is chronically ill for 50 days, recovers, and is chronically ill again for 40 days, all within 730 days, has accumulated 90 days and satisfies the elimination period. Had the second stretch fallen outside the 730-day window, the earlier 50 days would not count toward it.
